name: GO Classes Test Series 2023 | NIELIT Mock Test 1

question.text:
What are the last two digits of $1! + 2! + \dots +100!?$

  1. $00$
  2. $13$
  3. $30$
  4. $33$

If $a, b,$ and $c$ are three real numbers, then which of the following is not true?
  1. $\mid a+b \mid\leq \mid a \mid+\mid b \mid$
  2. $\mid a –b \mid \leq \mid a \mid + \mid b\mid$
  3. $\mid a-b \mid \leq \mid a \mid -\mid b \mid$
  4. $\mid a-c \mid \leq \mid a-b \mid+\mid b-c \mid$

The missing number in the given sequence $343,1331,$ ______$,\;4913$ is

  1. $3375$
  2. $2744$
  3. $2197$
  4. $4096$

In a new budget, the price of petrol rose by $25\%.$ By how much percent must a person reduce his consumption so that his expenditure on it does not increase?
  1. $10\%$
  2. $15\%$
  3. $20\%$
  4. $25\%$

If the ratio of the sides of two similar triangles is $3:5,$ what is the ratio of their areas?

  1. $3:5$
  2. $5:3$
  3. $9:25$
  4. $25:9$

In a certain code, $\text{‘CONSIDER’}$ is written as $\text{RMNBSFEJ},$ how is $\text{‘MONOPOLY’}$ written in that code?
  1. $\text{LNMNZMPQ}$
  2. $\text{NMNLZMPQ}$
  3. $\text{POPNXKNO}$
  4. $\text{NMNLXKNO}$

If a number is increased by $20 \%$ and then decreased by $15 \%$, what is the net percentage change?
  1. $2 \%$ increase
  2. $2 \%$ decrease
  3. $5 \%$ increase
  4. $5 \%$ decrease

In a certain coding system $\text{MOTHER}$ is coded as $\text{PQWJHT},$ how will you code $\text{SISTER}?$

  1. $\text{VKUVHT}$
  2. $\text{VKVVHU}$
  3. $\text{VKVVHT}$
  4. $\text{VKVVHS}$

The arithmetic mean of five different natural numbers is $12$. The largest possible value among the numbers is
  1. $12$
  2. $40$
  3. $50$
  4. $60$

If the population of a town is $p$ in the beginning of any year then it becomes $3+2p$ in the beginning of the next year. If the population in the beginning of $2019$ is $1000$, then the population in the beginning of $2034$ will be
  1. $(997)2^{14}+3$
  2. $(1003)^{15}+6$
  3. $(1003)2^{15}-3$
  4. $(997)^{15}-3$

Given $10$ tosses of a coin with the probability of head $ = 0.4 = (1 -$ the probability of tail$),$ the probability of at least one head is?

  1. $(0.4)^{10}$
  2. $1 - (0.4)^{10}$
  3. $1 - (0.6)^{10}$
  4. $(0.6)^{10}$

The expression $\dfrac{(x+y) - |x-y|}{2}$ is equal to :
A. The maximum of $x$ and $y$
b. The minimum of $x$ and $y$
C. $1$
D. None of the above

Let $x, y$ and $z$ be distinct integers, that are odd and positive. Which one of the following statements cannot be true?
  1. $xyz^2$ is odd.
  2. $(x - y)^2 z$ is even.
  3. $(x + y - z)^2 (x + y)$ is even.
  4. $(x - y) (y + z) (x + y - z)$ is odd

How many numbers are there between $99$ and $1000$ having at least one of their digits $7?$

  1. $250$
  2. $251$
  3. $252$
  4. $253$

A suitcase weighs one kilogram plus half of its weight. How much does the suitcase weigh?
  1. $1.3333$... kilograms
  2. $1.5$ kilograms
  3. $1.666$... kilograms
  4. $2$ kilograms

Introducing a boy, a girl said, "He is the son of the daughter of the father of my uncle." How is the boy related to the girl?
  1. Cousin
  2. Nephew
  3. Uncle
  4. Son-in-law

If the length of a rectangle is doubled and the width is tripled, by what factor does the area increase?

  1. $3$
  2. $4$
  3. $6$
  4. $9$

A sum of money doubles at compound interest in $6$ years. In how many years it will become $16$ times?

  1. $16$ years
  2. $24$ years
  3. $48$ years
  4. $96$ years

There are four bus routes between $\mathrm{A}$ and $\mathrm{B}$; and three bus routes between $\mathrm{B}$ and $\mathrm{C}$. A man can travel round-trip in a number of ways by bus from $\mathrm{A}$ to $\mathrm{C}$ via $\mathrm{B}$. If he does not want to use a bus route more than once, in how many ways can he make a round trip?

  1. $72$
  2. $144$
  3. $14$
  4. $19$

Two pipes $\text{A}$ and $\text{B}$ are attached to an empty water tank. Pipe $\text{A}$ fills the tank while pipe $\text{B}$ drains it. If pipe $\text{A}$ is opened at $2 \; \text{pm}$ and pipe $\text{B}$ is opened at $3 \; \text{pm},$ then the tank becomes full at $10 \; \text{pm}.$ Instead, if pipe $\text{A}$ is opened at $2 \; \text{pm}$ and pipe $\text{B}$ is opened at $4 \; \text{pm},$ then the tank becomes full at $6 \; \text{pm}.$ If pipe $\text{B}$ is not opened at all, then the time, in minutes, taken to fill the tank is
  1. $140$
  2. $264$
  3. $144$
  4. $120$

If $f(x)=x^2$ and $g(x)=\log _e x,$ then $f(x)+g(x)$ will be

  1. Even function
  2. Odd function
  3. Both
  4. None of the above

The difference between the compound interest and the simple interest earned at the end of $3^{\text{rd}}$ year on a sum of money at a rate of $10\%$ per annum is Rs. $77.5.$ What is the sum?

  1. Rs. $3,500$
  2. Rs. $2,500$
  3. Rs. $3,000$
  4. Rs. $2,000$

Answer the question on the basis of the data given below:

  •  $\text{O}$ is $\text{X’s}$ father
  •  $\text{Y}$ is $\text{Z’s}$ mother
  •  $\text{P}$ is $\text{O’s}$ mother
  •  $\text{X}$ is $\text{Z’s}$ Sister

How is $\text{O}$ related to $\text{Z}?$

  1. Brother
  2. Cousin
  3. Father
  4. Uncle

In a group of people, $30 \%$ can speak English, $40 \%$ can speak French, and $20 \%$ can speak both languages. What percentage of the group can speak at least one of the two languages?

  1. $30 \%$
  2. $40 \%$
  3. $50 \%$
  4. $60 \%$

A man travels three-fifths of distance $\text{AB}$ at a speed of $3 a$, and the remaining at a speed of $2 b$. If he goes from $\text{B}$ to $\text{A}$ and back at a speed of $5 c$ in the same time, then:

  1. $1 / a+1 / b=1 / c$
  2. $a+b=c$
  3. $1 / a+1 / b=2 / c$
  4. None of these

What is the next number in the sequence $: 2, 5, 10, 17,$ _________

  1. $24$
  2. $26$
  3. $29$
  4. $32$

In a $2 \times 4$ rectangle grid shown below, each cell is a rectangle. How many rectangles can be observed in the grid?
$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline{\;\;\;}&{\;\;\;}&{\;\;\;}&{\;\;\;}\\\hline{}&{}&{}&\\\hline\end{array}$$
  1. $21$
  2. $27$
  3. $30$
  4. $36$

Given a semicircle with $\text{O}$ as the centre, as shown in the figure, the ratio $\dfrac{\overline{\text{AC}}+\overline{\text{CB}}}{\overline{\text{AB}}}$ is ______, where $\overline{\text{AC}},\overline{\text{CB}}$ and $\overline{\text{AB}}$ are chords.

  1. $\sqrt{2}$
  2. $\sqrt{3}$
  3. $2$
  4. $3$

Look carefully for the pattern, and then choose which pair of numbers comes next
$$17 \: 17 \: 34 \: 20 \: 20 \: 31 \: 23$$

  1. $26 \: 23$
  2. $23 \: 33$
  3. $27 \: 28$
  4. $23 \: 28$

Ten friends planned to share equally the cost of buying a gift for their teacher. When two of them decided not to contribute, each of the other friends had to pay Rs. $150$ more. The cost of the gift was Rs. _____
  1. $666$
  2. $3000$
  3. $6000$
  4. $12000$

If the list of letters $\text{P, R, S, T, U}$ is an arithmetic sequence, which of the following are also in an arithmetic sequence?

  1. $\text{2P, 2R, 2S, 2T, 2U}$
  2. $\text{P-3, R-3, S-3, T-3, U-3}$
  3. $\text{P}^2, \text{R}^2, \text{S}^2, \text{T}^2, \text{U}^2$

 

  1. I only
  2. I and II
  3. II and III
  4. I and III

$\text{A}$ can complete a piece of work in $4$ days. $\text{B}$ takes double the time taken by $\text{A, C}$ takes double that of $\text{B},$ and $\text{D}$ takes double that of $\text{C}$ to complete the same task. They are paired in groups of two each. One pair takes two-thirds the time needed by the second pair to complete the work. Which is the first pair?
  1. $\text{A, B}$
  2. $\text{A, C}$
  3. $\text{B, C}$
  4. $\text{A, D}$

If $\text{A}$ can do a piece of work in $10$ days and $\text{B}$ can do the same work in $15$ days, how long will it take for them to complete the work together?

  1. $4$ days
  2. $5$ days
  3. $6$ days
  4. $7$ days

In how many ways $3$ scholarships can be awarded to $4$ applicants, when each applicant can receive any number of scholarships?
  1. $4$
  2. $12$
  3. $64$
  4. $81$

The natural numbers are divided into groups as $(1), (2,3,4), (5,6,7,8,9), \dots $ and so on. Then, the sum of the numbers in the $15 \text{th}$ group is equal to
  1. $6090$
  2. $4941$
  3. $6119$
  4. $7471$

Each of the following problems consists of a question and the statements labelled $(1)$ and $(2)$. You must decide whether the data given for the statements are sufficient to answer the questions.

If $n$ is an integer, is $n$ even?

  1. $2n$ is an even integer.
  2. $n - 1$ is an odd integer.

 

  1. Statement $(1)$ ALONE is sufficient, but statement $(2)$ alone is not sufficient.
  2. Statement $(2)$ ALONE is sufficient, but statement $(1)$ alone is not sufficient.
  3. BOTH statements TOGETHER are sufficient, but NEITHER statement alone is sufficient.
  4. EACH statement ALONE is sufficient.

There are three dice as shown below. What number will be opposite to the side bearing number two?

Options:-

  1. $4$    
  2. $3$        
  3. $6$       
  4. $5$

Study the following information carefully and answer the question:

Group of girls’ gossip with each other. All are sitting surrounding a round table. The name of the girls are Shiksha, radha, Chinu, snigdha and Rani. It is not necessary that they are sitting in the order of the name as mentioned here. Radha is second to the right of Shiksha. Shiksha doesn’t sit with Chinu. Rani is second to the right of Radha. Radha sits near Snigdha.

Who sits to the left of Shiksha?

  1. Rani
  2. Radha
  3. Chinu
  4. Snigdha

If $3 / 4$ of a number is subtracted from $5 / 8$ of the same number, the result is $6.$ What is the number?

  1. $32$
  2. $40$
  3. $48$
  4. $56$

Let $n$ be the number of different $5$ digit numbers, divisible by $4$ with the digits $1, 2, 3, 4, 5$ and $6,$ no digit being repeated in the numbers. What is the value of $n?$
  1. $144$
  2. $168$
  3. $192$
  4. None of these

In a class of $40$ students, $60\%$ are girls. How many boys are there in the class?

  1. $10$
  2. $12$
  3. $14$
  4. $16$

How many degrees apart are the minute hand and the hour hand of a clock at $4: 15?$
  1. $35.5^{\circ}$
  2. $30^{\circ}$
  3. $37.5^{\circ}$
  4. $32.5^{\circ}$

If $A$ and $B$ are two related events, and $P(A \mid B)$ represents the conditional probability, Bayes’ theorem states that
  1. $P(A\mid B) = \dfrac{P(A)}{P(B)} P(B\mid A)$
  2. $P(A\mid B) = P(A) P(B) P(B\mid A)$
  3. $P(A\mid B) = \dfrac{P(A)}{P(B)}$
  4. $P(A\mid B) = P(A)+P(B)$

The switch $\text{SPST}$ is closed at $t=0$. Find $\dfrac{d i(0^+)}{d t}$

  1. $0$
  2. $40$
  3. $50$
  4. None

In how many ways can $10$ examination papers be arranged so that the best and the worst papers never come together?

  1. $8 \times 9!$ 
  2. $8 \times 8!$ 
  3. $7 \times 9 !$
  4. $9 \times 8!$

A random communication signal has the following pdf
$$\rho(x)=a e^{-b|x|}, \forall x,-\infty<x<+\infty$$

The ratio $a / b$ will be equal to

  1. $2$
  2. $1$
  3. $1 / 2$
  4. $6$

Which protocol is used for transmitting email over the Internet?
  1. HTTP
  2. FTP
  3. MTP
  4. DNS

Which of the following propositions is a tautology?
  1. $(p\lor q)\to q$
  2. $p\lor (q\to p)$
  3. $p\lor (p\to q)$
  4. Both (B) and (C)

Suppose that $ ext{S}$ and $ ext{T}$ are sets. Which of the following first-order logic statements are translations of the statement $ ext{“S}$ is not a subset of $ ext{T”}?$
  1. $ orall x .(x \in ext{S} ightarrow x otin ext{T})$
  2. $ orall x .(x \in ext{S} \wedge x otin ext{T})$
  3. $\exists x .(x \in ext{S} ightarrow x otin ext{T})$
  4. $\exists x .(x \in ext{S} \wedge x otin ext{T})$

A CPU has $32$-bit instructions. A program starts at address $1000$ (in decimal). Which one of the following is a valid program counter (PC) for this program?

  1. $1101$
  2. $1207$
  3. $1300$
  4. $1406$

If $(1+i)^{100}=2^{49}(x+i y)$ then $x^2+y^2=$

  1. $2$
  2. $4$
  3. $8$
  4. $16$

$$\displaystyle \int_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}} \sin^{7}\theta \cos ^{4} \theta d\theta=?$$

  1. $16/1155$
  2. $16/385$
  3. $16\pi/385$
  4. $8\pi/385$

• Statement (I): BJT is a current controlled device.
  • Statement (II): The current carriers in a BJT are either holes or electrons.
  1. Both assertion and reason are true and reason is correct explanation of assertion
  2. Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not correct explanation of assertion
  3. Assertion is true but reason is false
  4. Assertion is false but reason is true

The function $f(x)=x^{5}-5x^{4}+5x^{3}-1$ has
  1. one minima and two maxima
  2. two minima and one maxima
  3. two minima and two maxima
  4. one minima and one maxima

Two eigenvalues of a $3\times3$ real matrix $P$ are $(2+ \sqrt-1)$ and $3$. The determinant of $P$ is _______.
  1. $0$
  2. $1$
  3. $15$
  4. $-1$

A sequential circuit using $\text{D}$ Flip-Flop and logic gates is shown in the figure, where $\text{X}$ and $\text{Y}$ are the inputs and $\text{Z}$ is the output. The circuit is

  1. $\text{S-R}$ Flip-Flop with inputs $\text{X=R}$ and $\text{Y=S}$
  2. $\text{S-R}$ Flip-Flop with inputs $\text{X=S}$ and $\text{Y=R}$
  3. $\text{J-K}$ Flip-Flop with inputs $\text{X=J}$ and $\text{Y=K}$
  4. $\text{J-K}$ Flip-Flop with inputs $\text{X=K}$ and $\text{Y=J}$

The eigenvalues of the matrix $\begin{bmatrix}1 & 2\\ 4 & 3 \end{bmatrix}$ are
  1. $\text{5 and -5}$
  2. $\text{5 and -1}$
  3. $\text{1 and -5}$
  4. $\text{2 and 3}$

Let $A$ and $B$ be sets with cardinalities $m$ and $n$ respectively. The number of one-one mappings from $A$ to $B$, when $m < n,$ is

  1. $m^n$
  2. $^nP_m$
  3. $^nC_m$
  4. $^mP_n$

Consider the following function definition.

void greet(int n)
{
    if(n>0)
    {
        printf("hello");
        greet(n-1);
    }
    printf("world");
}

If you run $\textsf{greet(n)}$ for some non-negative integer $\textsf{n},$ what would it print?

  1. $\textsf{n}$ times "hello", followed by $\textsf{n+1}$ times "world"
  2. $\textsf{n}$ times "hello", followed by $\textsf{n}$ times "world"
  3. $\textsf{n}$ times "helloworld"
  4. $\textsf{n+1}$ times "helloworld"

Which one is the correct translation of the following statement into mathematical logic?
“None of my friends are perfect.”
  1. $ eg\:\exists\:x(p(x)\land q(x))$
  2. $\exists\:x( eg\:p(x)\land q(x))$
  3. $\exists\:x( eg\:p(x)\land eg\:q(x))$
  4. $\exists\:x(p(x)\land eg\:q(x))$

What is the primary goal of software testing?

  1. To eliminate all bugs from the software
  2. To validate the correctness of the software
  3. To measure the software complexity
  4. To reduce software performance

For the set $N$ of natural numbers and a binary operation $f : N \times N \to N,$ an element $z \in N$ is called an identity for $f,$ if $f (a, z) = a = f(z, a),$ for all $a \in N.$ Which of the following binary operations have an identity?
  1. $f (x, y) = x + y - 3$
  2. $f (x, y) = \max(x, y)$
  3. $f (x, y) = x^y$

  1. I and II only
  2. II and III only
  3. I and III only
  4. None of these

Let $A, B$, and $C$ be sets. Which of the following statements represents the De Morgan's Law correctly?
  1. $(A \cap B)^{\prime}=A^{\prime} \cap B^{\prime}$
  2. $(A \cup B)^{\prime}=A^{\prime} \cup B^{\prime}$
  3. $(A \cap B)^{\prime}=A^{\prime} \cup B^{\prime}$
  4. $(A \cup B)^{\prime}=A^{\prime} \cap B$

Which data structure uses LIFO (Last-In-First-Out) ordering?
  1. Queue
  2. Stack
  3. Linked List
  4. Binary Tree

The output voltage $\left(V_0\right)$ for the circuit is


When (i) $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{i}_1}=10 \mathrm{~V},$ (ii) $\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{i}_2}=5 \mathrm{~V}$
 

  1. $\mathrm{V}_{0_1}=5 \mathrm{~V}, \mathrm{~V}_{0_2}=\frac{20}{6} \mathrm{~V}$
  2. $\mathrm{V}_{0_1}=5 \mathrm{~V}, \mathrm{~V}_{0_2}=\frac{20}{3} \mathrm{~V}$
  3. $\mathrm{V}_{0_1}=10 \mathrm{~V}, \quad \mathrm{~V}_{\mathrm{0}_2}=5 \mathrm{~V}$
  4. None

For a periodic waveform to be half-wave symmetric it must be represented by a function satisfying
  1. $f(t)=f(t+T / 2)$
  2. $f(t)=-f(t+T / 2)$
  3. $f(t)=f-(-t)$
  4. $f(t)=f(-t)$

What is a tree?
  1. A connected graph with no cycles.
  2. A graph with exactly four vertices.
  3. A graph with at least one cycle.
  4. A graph with no vertices.

The open loop transfer function of a unity negative feedback control system is given by,
$$
G(s)=\frac{10}{s(0.4 s+1)(0.15 s+1)}
$$
The steady-state error when it is subjected to the input $(5+3 t) u(t)$ is

  1. $0$
  2. $0.1$
  3. $0.3$
  4. $\infty$

What is the minimum number of edges required to form a connected graph with n vertices?

  1. $0$
  2. $n-1$
  3. $n$
  4. $n+1$

Which normal form eliminates partial dependencies?

  1. First Normal Form $\text{(1NF)}$
  2. Second Normal Form $\text{(2NF)}$
  3. Third Normal Form $\text{(3NF)}$
  4. Boyce-Codd Normal Form $\text{(BCNF)}$

The running time of an algorithm $T(n),$ where $’n’$ is the input size , is given by

$T(n) = 8T(n/2) + qn,$ if $n>1$
$\qquad\; = p,$ if $n = 1$

Where $p,q$ are constants. The order of this algorithm is

  1. $n^{2}$
  2. $n^{n}$
  3. $n^{3}$
  4. $n$

Consider three vectors $x=\begin{bmatrix}1\\2 \end{bmatrix}, y=\begin{bmatrix}4\\8 \end{bmatrix},z=\begin{bmatrix}3\\1 \end{bmatrix}$. Which of the following statements is true
  1. $x$ and $y$ are linearly independent
  2. $x$ and $y$ are linearly dependent
  3. $x$ and $z$ are linearly dependent
  4. $y$ and $z$ are linearly dependent

What is the maximum number of edges in a directed graph with $n$ nodes?
  1. $n - 1$
  2. $n$
  3. $n^2$
  4. $(n^2 - n)$

Given the truth table of a Binary Operation $\$$ as follows:
$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|} \hline {}  \text{X} & \text{Y}& \text{X\$Y}\\\hline \text{1} & \text{0}& \text{1}\\\hline \text{1} & \text{1}& \text{1}\\\hline \text{0} & \text{1}& \text{0}\\ \hline \text{0} & \text{0}& \text{1}\\\hline \end{array}$$
Identify the matching Boolean Expression.

  1. $X \$ \neg Y$
  2. $\neg X \$ Y$
  3. $\neg X \$ \neg Y$
  4. none of the options

What is the purpose of a firewall in a computer network?
  1. To prevent unauthorized access
  2. To regulate network traffic
  3. To block malicious software
  4. To encrypt data transmission

Which CPU scheduling algorithm provides the highest average turnaround time?
  1. First-Come, First-Served (FCFS)
  2. Shortest Job Next (SJN)
  3. Round Robin (RR)
  4. Priority Scheduling

In how many ways can $8$ Indians and, $4$ American and $4$ Englishmen can be seated in a row so that all person of the same nationality sit together?

  1. $3! 4 ! 8 ! 4 !$
  2. $3! 8 !$
  3. $4 ! 4!$ 
  4. $8 ! 4 ! 4 !$

Avalanche breakdown in a semiconductor diode occurs when
  1. the potential barrier is reduced to zero
  2. forward current exceeds a certain value
  3. forward bias exceeds a certain value
  4. reverse bias exceeds a certain value

Fourier transform of $\dfrac{t}{\left(1+t^2\right)^2}$ is

  1. $-\mathrm{j~} \pi^2 \mathrm{~f} \mathrm{~e}^{-|\omega|}$
  2. $-\mathrm{j~} \omega \mathrm{~e~}^{-|\omega|}$
  3. $\mathrm{j~} \pi \mathrm{~f} \mathrm{~e}^{-|\mathrm{f}|}$
  4. $\mathrm{j~} \mathrm{f}^2 \mathrm{~e}^{-|\mathrm{f}|}$

Which of the following integer sequence if used as a degree sequence would represent a simple graph?

  1. $(8,8,6,5,5,5,4,4,3,3,2,2,0)$
  2. $(7,7,6,5,5,4,3,3,3,3,2,1)$
  3. $(1,1,1,2,2,2,3,3,4,4,4,5,5)$
  4. $(7,7,6,6,5,5,4,4,3,3,2,2,1,1)$

In set theory, which of the following statements correctly defines the power set of a set $\text{A}?$

  1. The set containing all elements of $\text{A}$ and their subsets.
  2. The set containing all subsets of $\text{A}.$
  3. The set containing the union of $\text{A}$ and its subsets.
  4. The set containing the intersection of $\text{A}$ and its subsets.

Let $A$ and $B$ be two sets. Which of the following statements is true regarding the union of their complements, denoted as $(A \cup B)^{\prime}?$
  1. $(A \cup B)^{\prime}=A^{\prime} \cup B^{\prime}$
  2. $(A \cup B)^{\prime}=A^{\prime} \cap B^{\prime}$
  3. $(A \cup B)^{\prime}=A^{\prime} \cap B$
  4. $(A \cup B)^{\prime}=A \cap B^{\prime}$

The probability that the top and bottom cards of a randomly shuffled deck are both aces is:

  1. $4/52\times 4/52$
  2. $4/52\times 3/52$
  3. $4/52\times 3/51$
  4. $4/52\times 4/51$

Let $A$ and $B$ be sets and let $A^c$ and $B^c$ denote the complements of the sets $A$ and $B$. The set $(A-B) \cup (B-A) \cup (A \cap B)$ is equal to
  1. $A \cup B$
  2. $A^c \cup B^c$
  3. $A \cap B$
  4. $A^c \cap B^c$
